questions.question: When are rollovers most likely to happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. Drivers should slow down before entering turns and curves, especially when pulling a full load.

questions.question: All trailers made after what year must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: What does pushing in the trailer air supply control do?
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to supply air to the trailer. Pull out the control to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: What do you test by pulling out the trailer air supply control?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before starting a trip. First, make sure the trailer rolls freely. Then pull out the trailer air supply control or set it to "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The trailer service air line is also called the control line or signal line.

questions.question: Which vehicle is most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to roll over from the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer is too high?
questions.explanation: Before coupling a tractor and trailer, check that the trailer is at the proper height. If the trailer is too low, the nose may be damaged. If the trailer is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: If a trailer starts to jackknife, what should you not do?

options.text: Allow the wheels to grip the road.
Allow the trailer to straighten out.

questions.explanation: If a trailer starts to jackknife, release the brakes and let the wheels regain grip on the road. Do not apply the trailer hand brake. Applying brakes caused the skid in the first place and will only make it worse.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A device that keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
A device that controls fuel levels.
A device that helps the battery recharge.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
questions.explanation: On combination vehicles with air brakes, the tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer develops a leak or breaks away from the tractor.

questions.question: How do you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Test the tractor protection valve by letting the air system charge fully, turning off the engine, then pressing the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to the emergency position when air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: What should you do after finishing a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Leave the emergency line valve open.
Leave the rear shut-off valves open.

questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check for escaping air. This makes sure air reaches all brakes on all trailers. Close both shut-off valves before you start to drive.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: Only when the trailer is carrying a load
Only to test the trailer's brakes
Only in bad weather when the trailer may skid

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer's brakes
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) is used to test the trailer brakes only. Using it while driving can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand brake during a trailer jackknife?
questions.explanation: If the trailer starts to jackknife, release the brakes to help your tires regain traction. Using the trailer hand brake during a skid will make the skid worse.

questions.question: Before backing your tractor under the trailer, the trailer brakes must be:
questions.explanation: When coupling trailers, you must lock the trailer brakes before backing your tractor under the trailer. This is an important safety step when operating a combination vehicle.

questions.question: If your vehicle was built before 1998 and you are not sure if it has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), how can you find out?

options.text: Check for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
Look for a red light on the front right corner of the converter dolly.
Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: For vehicles built before 1998, check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes to find out if it has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: How can you find out if a vehicle built before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
Check for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: For vehicles built before 1998, check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes to find out if it has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: What is the best way to know your trailer has started to skid?

options.text: Check the trailer in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the trailer in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: The best way to notice that your trailer has started to skid is to look at it in your mirrors. This lets you spot a skid early and respond quickly.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
When the driver in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
When a truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle is driven too fast. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low to the ground and take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: What should a driver do to prevent a rollover?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you turn too quickly. To prevent rollovers, keep the center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: If the trailer drifts off-course while you are backing, what should you do?

options.text: Return the steering wheel to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift to correct it right away.
